about: The inside of the large intestine, drawn as anatomy: the caecum with its appendix, the ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colon and the rectum, the three taeniae coli, the folds that mark the haustra, a mucosal lining and the faecal contents. Contents creep towards the rectum, and water is drawn from the lumen into the wall. It leaves out the rectal folds, the anal sphincters, the crypts, the gut bacteria and the movement of the haustra themselves. The model has no separate diarrhoea signal for this view, so faster transit is shown through the gut-motility signals, and the water stream thins when motility is raised. Activity bars are display indices, not measurements. The flexures, epiploic appendages, mesocolon, rectal folds, anal canal with its sphincters, and the cells of enlarged colonic crypts are drawn as finer structures; sizes and counts are schematic. The caecum and the descending and sigmoid colon are drawn clear of the iliac bones, so the iliacus can line the fossa between them; this raises the caecum above the end of the drawn ileum, which therefore stops short of the caecum's wall.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Caecum
parts.summary: Blind pouch at the start of the colon that receives the ileal chyme
parts.function: The caecum is the wide blind pouch below the ileocaecal junction. It receives liquid chyme from the ileum and begins the absorption of water and salts. The appendix opens from its lower end. It brightens as contents reach the colon.

drives.note: Contents reaching the colon arrive here first.
Chyme leaving the ileum is delivered to the caecum.

parts.label: Appendix
parts.summary: Narrow blind tube off the caecum with lymphoid tissue in its wall
parts.function: The vermiform appendix is a narrow blind-ended tube that opens from the caecum. Its wall is rich in lymphoid tissue and it takes part in mucosal immunity. It brightens when the simulator reports immune activation or infection.

drives.note: Lymphoid tissue in its wall responds to immune activation.
A pathogen burden engages gut-associated lymphoid tissue.

parts.label: Ascending Colon
parts.summary: Rises on the right; absorbs much of the water and salt
parts.function: The ascending colon passes up the right side of the abdomen to the right colic flexure. Its contents are still fluid, and it is where most water and salt absorption takes place. It brightens with colonic transit and with the mucosal absorption of water.

drives.note: Contents in the colon mean the segment is working.
Raised gut motility moves contents through faster.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits colonic motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale, not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Transverse Colon
parts.summary: Crosses the abdomen from right to left; the most mobile part
parts.function: The transverse colon crosses the abdomen between the right and left colic flexures, hanging on its own mesentery. Water absorption continues here and the contents become more solid. Mass movements that sweep contents along begin in this segment. It brightens with colonic transit.

drives.note: Contents in the colon mean the segment is working.
Raised gut motility moves contents through faster.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits colonic motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale, not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Descending Colon
parts.summary: Runs down the left side and stores the formed stool
parts.function: The descending colon runs down the left side of the abdomen. It is narrower than the ascending colon and mainly stores and conducts faecal matter towards the sigmoid. It brightens with colonic transit.

drives.note: Contents in the colon mean the segment is working.
Raised gut motility moves contents through faster.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits colonic motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale, not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Sigmoid Colon
parts.summary: S-shaped loop that leads to the rectum
parts.function: The sigmoid colon is an S-shaped loop between the descending colon and the rectum. Its strong muscle holds the stool and moves it on into the rectum. It brightens with colonic transit.

drives.note: Contents in the colon mean the segment is working.
Raised gut motility moves contents through faster.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits colonic motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale, not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Rectum
parts.summary: Final straight part; holds stool until it is passed
parts.function: The rectum is the last part of the large bowel, ending in the anal canal. It stretches to hold stool until it is passed, and has no haustra or separate taeniae. It brightens with colonic transit.

drives.note: Contents reaching the end of the colon collect here.
Parasympathetic outflow from the sacral cord drives emptying.

parts.label: Taeniae Coli
parts.summary: Three longitudinal muscle bands that gather the colon into pouches
parts.function: The taeniae coli are three bands of longitudinal smooth muscle that run along the colon from the caecum to the rectum. Because they are shorter than the bowel they gather it into pouches, the haustra. They brighten with gut motility.

drives.note: Raised motility is carried out by this muscle.
Reduced motility quietens it.
Parasympathetic outflow excites colonic smooth muscle.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits colonic motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale, not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Haustra
parts.summary: Semilunar folds between the pouches of the colon wall
parts.function: Haustra are the sacculations of the colon wall. Each is separated from the next by a semilunar fold, drawn here as a ring. Contractions of the haustra slowly knead the contents, which exposes them to the lining so that water can be absorbed. They brighten with colonic transit and motility.

drives.note: Contents in the colon are kneaded by haustral contractions.
Raised motility increases haustral activity.

parts.label: Faecal Contents
parts.summary: Solid and semi-solid contents moving slowly towards the rectum
parts.function: The contents of the colon are the undigested residue, bacteria and the water not yet absorbed. They move slowly, with occasional mass movements. They are drawn as a string of masses that brightens with the amount of material in the colon.

drives.note: More material in the colon means more contents to show.
Faster motility carries contents along sooner.

parts.label: Mucosa
parts.summary: Lining that absorbs water and salts from the contents
parts.function: The colonic mucosa is the lining that absorbs water and electrolytes from the contents and secretes mucus to lubricate their passage. The more slowly the contents travel the more water is taken back. It brightens with colonic transit and dims when motility is raised, because faster transit leaves less time for absorption.

drives.note: Contents in the colon give the lining something to absorb.
Faster transit leaves less time for water absorption.
Slower transit allows more water to be absorbed.

parts.label: Hepatic (Right Colic) Flexure
parts.summary: The bend where the ascending colon turns into the transverse colon, beneath the liver
parts.function: At the hepatic flexure the colon turns from running upward to running across the abdomen. It lies close to the liver.

drives.note: Contents in the colon mean the segment is working.
Raised gut motility moves contents through faster.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits colonic motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale, not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Splenic (Left Colic) Flexure
parts.summary: The bend where the transverse colon turns into the descending colon, near the spleen
parts.function: At the splenic flexure the colon turns downward again to become the descending colon. It lies close to the spleen and is usually higher than the hepatic flexure.

drives.note: Contents in the colon mean the segment is working.
Raised gut motility moves contents through faster.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits colonic motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale, not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Epiploic Appendages
parts.summary: Small fat-filled tags of peritoneum hanging from the surface of the colon
parts.function: The appendages are small pouches of fat covered by peritoneum along the colon, apart from the rectum. They are a landmark that distinguishes colon from small bowel. Their number and position here are schematic.

parts.label: Mesocolon
parts.summary: The fold of peritoneum that suspends the transverse and sigmoid colon
parts.function: The transverse and sigmoid mesocolons attach those parts of the colon to the back wall of the abdomen and carry their vessels and nerves. They are drawn as flat fans, not the real fatty folds.

parts.label: Rectal Transverse Folds
parts.summary: Crescent-shaped folds that project into the lumen of the rectum
parts.function: The rectum has several transverse folds on alternating sides that project into its lumen. They are thought to support the contents of the rectum. Three are drawn.

drives.note: Contents reaching the rectum collect against them.

parts.label: Anal Canal
parts.summary: The short terminal part of the bowel, ending at the anus
parts.function: The anal canal is the last part of the gut. It is closed by its sphincters except when faeces are passed.

drives.note: Contents reaching the end of the colon press on it.
Parasympathetic outflow from the sacral cord drives emptying.

parts.label: Anal Columns
parts.summary: Longitudinal folds of the lining in the upper anal canal
parts.function: The anal columns are vertical ridges of mucosa in the upper part of the canal. Each contains small branches of the rectal vessels.

parts.label: Pectinate (Dentate) Line
parts.summary: The ragged line marking the lower ends of the anal valves
parts.function: The pectinate line marks where the lining of the upper canal meets that of the lower canal. Above it the nerve supply and the drainage of blood and lymph differ from those below it.

parts.label: Internal Anal Sphincter
parts.summary: The inner ring of smooth muscle around the anal canal
parts.function: The internal anal sphincter is a thickening of the circular smooth muscle of the gut wall. It is not under voluntary control and is closed most of the time.

drives.note: Parasympathetic outflow relaxes it to allow emptying.

parts.label: External Anal Sphincter
parts.summary: The outer ring of skeletal muscle around the anal canal
parts.function: The external anal sphincter is skeletal muscle and so can be closed at will. It surrounds the internal sphincter and gives voluntary control over emptying.

parts.label: Colonic Crypts
parts.summary: Straight tubular pits that make up the lining of the colon
parts.function: The colon has no villi. Its lining is a sheet of closely packed straight crypts whose cells renew from stem cells at the base. Two enlarged crypts are drawn on the wall of the ascending colon.

parts.label: Goblet Cells
parts.summary: Mucus-secreting cells, very numerous in the colon
parts.function: Goblet cells line the crypts and make the mucus that lubricates the passage of faeces. Their share of the lining is larger in the colon than elsewhere in the gut.

drives.note: Contents in the colon call for lubrication.

parts.label: Colonocytes
parts.summary: The absorbing surface cells of the colon
parts.function: Colonocytes are the columnar cells of the colon's surface. They absorb water and salts from the contents, which firms the faeces.

drives.note: Contents in the colon give the lining something to absorb.
Faster transit leaves less time for water absorption.
Slower transit allows more water to be absorbed.
